title: The Unsent, Core Sample
statement: Ingrid asked for a core, and a core is a mosaic by nature: one tile per year, in order, with nothing left out. I cut a narrow strip from Mara's cross-section, top to bottom through the pith, and set it on the field to the right of the vessel as a column of thirty-five bands, dark where the ring was dark, pale where the growth was easy, each band slightly different in height because the years were. The slot it came from stays open in the vessel, a thin line of night from rim to rim. Now the archive can be read by anyone who can count, without touching the thing that holds it. The next hand can read it, or take a second core and compare.
process: I kept the parent's dusk field, wooden vessel, thirty-five rings and dark pith, cut a vertical slot through the vessel on the right of centre, and built the core as a column of thirty-five stacked rectangles whose heights follow the ring spacing of the parent, with a tick mark and a faint number-free scale beside it. The slot is lined with the same dark as the pith.

proposal.direction: Take a core sample. Cut a narrow vertical strip out of the rings and set it beside the vessel on the field, so the thirty-five rings can be read in a straight line like a ruler, and leave the slot in the vessel where it came from.
proposal.rationale: A core is how you read a trunk without felling it; the room agreed the archive should be able to read its own age without destroying the thing that holds it.
